Oh man, I have this too! Not for the same reason likely but same symptom, comes back toward the end of the work week since I drive for a living. I'm pretty fit now but I was disabled in my right leg for 15 years until carnivore lowered inflammation enough that my right hip released a trapped sciatic nerve that had me hobbling entirely on my left leg that whole time. That leg got extremely atrophied, and the fascia stiffened up and adhered, so every time I exercised it, it aggravated the area and caused swelling and water retention you could see on the scale and physically. I'd take a few days off with my feet up, too sore to move, and during those rest nights I'd pee constantly and lose a ton of weight. It took over 3 years as a carnivore plus exercise before I could jog even a little, and the inflammation keeps happening less and less.

When your fascia isn't loosened up yet, your lymphatic system can't drain properly through your legs, hips, and everywhere else, it relies on muscle movement to move fluid since it has no pump of its own. I've had big leaps in healing from uncomfortable hip-loosening moves I found on YouTube, one is basically the pap smear position, sitting with knees dropped all the way to one side so your right knee touches the bottom of your left foot, then reversing sides. That loosens the hips and gets a lot more circulation going. Lying on your back with your butt against a wall and legs straight up for 30 minutes before bed helps a lot too. Jumping in place and shaking your whole body loose gets things moving as well. I recently started being able to pull my legs up behind me while standing, one at a time, for a good front-of-thigh stretch, now I catch myself doing it just standing in line at the grocery store.

I went to Turkey before any of this improved and that flight was brutal, so I sympathize big time. BTW, you look fantastic and your energy is entirely different and awesome! It's so great to see. I love your whole family.
